To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the work of colleges is not well understood, (2) the work is a social action system, (3) there are four functional imperatives, and (4) norms are the key to understanding the work.
the normative structures of colleges and universities are in a state of flux and that the functional imperatives of the social action system of college and university work are being threatened.

(1) the normative structures of the social action system of college and university work are critical to the functional imperatives of the system, (2) these structures are not static but are in flux, and (3) the normative structure of the social action systems of college and university are not the same as those of the social action of other work systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the normative structure of the work of colleges.
the role of norms in the work of colleges.
the normative structure of colleges and universities and how it affects the functional imperatives of the social action systems of these institutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social action system of higher education is a complex system of interrelated and interdependent subsystems that are organized by normative structures.
the norms of the college and university system are critical for its functioning and that the functional imperative of integration is the most critical of all.
the social action system of college and university work is a normative social system that requires the development of a set of norms to guide the functional imperatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a shared understanding of the functional imperatives and the role of norms in their achievement, but we disagree about the nature of the normative structures and their sources.
the normative structures of colleges and universities are in a state of disrepair.
the normative structures of the social action system are the most important element of the system and are the most important determinant of the system's success or failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the normative structures of colleges and universities are not well aligned with the functional imperatives of the work of colleges, and that this misalignment has significant implications for the quality of the work of higher education.

the social action system of college and university work is not a system of pure technical rationality but rather a system in which the technical imperatives of the system are mediated and made possible by normative structures.
the social action system is a critical concept for understanding the nature and function of the college and university work system.
